==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈwɔːd/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈwɔːd/|/ɹəˈwɔːd/|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈwɔɹd/|/ɹəˈwɔɹd/|/ɹiˈwɔɹd/|a=GA,CA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-reward.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈwoːd/|/ɹəˈwoːd/|a=AU}} * {{IPA|en|/ɹəˈwoːd/|a=NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|ɔː(ɹ)d|s=2}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*wer-|id=heed}} From {{inh|en|enm|reward}}, {{m|enm|rewarde}}, from {{der|en|fro|reward||reward}} (compare {{cog|fro|regard}}, whence modern French {{m|fr|regard}}, and also English {{m|en|regard}} through Middle French), from {{m|fro|rewarder||to reward}} (compare {{cog|fro|reguarder}}), from {{m|fro|re-}} + {{m|fro|warder||to guard, keep}} (compare {{cog|fro|guarder}}); the Anglo-Norman forms are derived from {{der|en|fro-nor|-}} variants of Old French, ultimately of {{der|en|gem|-}} ({{der|en|frk|-}}) origin. Compare {{m|en|regard}}, {{m|en|warden}}, {{m|en|guard}}. See more below. Mostly displaced {{ncog|ang|mēd}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|meed}}. Displaced {{ncog|ang|lēan}} and {{m|ang|edlēan}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # Something of [[value]] given in return for an act. #: {{synonyms|en|payment|recompense|tithing|meed}} #: {{antonyms|en|penalty|punishment}} #: {{ux|en|For catching the thief, you'll get a nice '''reward'''.}} # A [[prize]] promised for a certain deed or catch #: {{syn|en|bounty}} #: {{ux|en|The '''rewards''' for bringing in badly wanted criminals are printed on 'dead or alive' posters.}} # {{lb|en|Christianity|,|with|possessive|_|pronoun}} one's place in [[heaven]]; God's judgment in the afterlife; death #* {{RQ:KJV|book=Revelation|chapter=22|verse=12|passage=And behold, I come quickly, and my '''reward''' is with mee, to giue euery man according as his worke shall be.|brackets=on}} #* '''2007''', ''{{w|No Country for Old Men}}'' by {{w|Coen brothers|Joel and Ethen Coen}}: #*: {{quote|en|Your daddy ever tell you how Uncle Mac come to his '''reward'''?}} # The [[result]] of an [[action]], whether good or bad. #: {{syn|en|consequence}} #: {{ux|en|Is this the '''reward''' I get for telling the truth: to be put in jail?}} #* {{quote-web |en |date=January 22, 2013 |author=Phil McNulty |title=Aston Villa 2-1 Bradford (3-4) |work=BBC |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/21022502 |page= |passage=Christian Benteke's first-half goal was just '''reward''' for Villa's undoubted superiority but Bradford managed to survive without further damage until half-time, before scoring the goal that takes them to Wembley for the first time since 1996.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160124024927/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/21022502|archivedate=24 January 2016}} =====Derived terms===== {{t-check|wyi|mabrim-boon-neen}} {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|rewarden}}, from {{der|en|xno|rewarder||to reward}}, from {{m|fro|re-}} + {{m|fro|warder||to guard, keep}}, from {{der|en|fro-nor}}, from {{der|en|frk|*wardēn|*wardōn|t=to guard, keep}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*wardōną||to guard, defend}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wer-||to cover, shelter, defend, guard, shut}}. Cognate with {{cog|osx|wardōn||to guard, provide for, protect}}, {{cog|ang|weardian||to guard}}, {{cog|goh|wartēn||to watch, keep, look after}}. More at {{l|en|ward}}. {{piecewise doublet|en|regard}}. Displaced {{ncog|ang|lēanian}}. In this sense, displaced {{ncog|ang|ġieldan}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|yield}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{senseid|en|give-a-reward}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To give a reward to or for. #: {{ux|en|Why are you '''rewarding''' the child for misbehaving?}} #: {{ux|en|Why are you '''rewarding''' that bad behaviour?}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To be a [[recompense]] for. #: {{ux|en|Decorations are meant to '''reward''' the most meritous acts and services.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 2, 2011|author=Phil McNulty|work=BBC |title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/14770875.stm Bulgaria 0-3 England] |passage=The Italian opted for Bolton's Cahill alongside captain John Terry - and his decision was '''rewarded''' with a goal after only 13 minutes. Bulgaria gave a hint of defensive frailties to come when they failed to clear Young's corner, and when Gareth Barry found Cahill in the box he applied the finish past Nikolay Mihaylov.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To [[give]] (something) as a reward. #* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|6.25|2|IV|xxvj|passage=Thenne syr Marhaus departed and within two dayes his damoysel brought hym where as was a grete tornement that the lady de Vawse has cryed
{{...}}
And there syr Marhaus dyd so nobly that he was renomed
& had somtyme doune fourty knyghtes
and soo the serklet of gold was '''rewarded''' hym}} #* {{RQ:KJV|1 Samuel|24|17|passage=Thou hast '''rewarded''' me good, whereas I have '''rewarded''' thee evil.}} =====Derived terms===== {{col4|en|misreward|overreward|rewardability|rewardee|nonrewarded|overrewarded|rewardedly|rewardedness|superrewarded|unrewarded |rewardable |rewarder |rewarding |unrewarded }} =====Related terms===== * {{l|en|award}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|give a reward to}} * Arabic: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Latgalian: * Latvian: * Macedonian: * Old English: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|награжда́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|награди́ть|pf}}, {{t+|ru|вознагражда́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|вознагради́ть|pf}}, {{qualifier|encourage}} {{t+|ru|поощря́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|поощри́ть|pf}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Shan: * Slovak: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Thai: * Turkish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-see|recompense|recompense}} ===Further reading=== * {{R:New English Dictionary|Reward|pos=''sb.''¹|noformat=yes|VIII|part=1|620}} * {{R:New English Dictionary|† Reward|pos=''sb.''²|noformat=yes|VIII|part=1|620|3}} * {{R:New English Dictionary|Reward|pos=v|VIII|part=1|pages=620–621|pageref=620|url=https://archive.org/details/oed8aarch/page/n633/mode/2up}} * {{R:New English Dictionary|† Rewa·rd|pos=pa. pple|VIII|part=1|621|1}} * {{R:Webster 1913}} * {{R:Century}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=aderrw|Warder|drawer|redraw|warder|warred}}
